Date: 2027-04-11T02:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Mismatched outputs in batch scoring runs — initial findings

Team — preliminary engineering findings (internal dry-run notes):

Executive technical summary:
- Root cause: a tokenizer migration deployed to a subset of servers (rollout ID rtkn-v2.4) introduced a subtle normalization change for emoji and certain unicode combining sequences. For many inputs the token boundaries shifted by 1 token which — for batched scoring with KV-cache reuse — produced different generation continuations in ~2–3% of cases.
- Secondary factor: a race in the KV cache refill logic when concurrent batch requests hit mixed-backend pools caused stale KV slices to be used for a small fraction of requests during the rollout window.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2027-04-10T15:52:00Z — rtkn-v2.4 rollout started (canary group)
- 2027-04-10T15:55:00Z — first tokenizer warning spikes detected in monitoring
- 2027-04-10T16:20:00Z — incident reflected in customer batch diffs (BlueWave sample timestamps)
- 2027-04-10T18:42:00Z — emergency rollback of rtkn-v2.4 to stable (rtkn-v2.3) completed across serving fleet
- 2027-04-10T18:50:00Z — KV cache hotfix (INF-7123) deployed to prevent stale-slice reuse

What we did:
- Rolled back tokenizer to rtkn-v2.3 (full rollback finished at 18:42 UTC).
- Deployed KV-cache sequencing fix (hotfix INF-7123) at 18:50 UTC.
- Reprocessed a subset of affected batch jobs for BlueWave and validated outputs against pre-incident baselines; mismatches reduced to <0.01%.

Immediate next steps (customer-facing items to include):
1) Share customer-facing RCA with timeline and affected-scope estimate.
2) Offer reprocessing support for impacted batch runs and share how to request it.
3) Provide audit logs for the affected window and verification checklist.
4) Propose compensatory credit for trouble and a 1:1 sync with engineering leads.

Longer-term mitigations:
- Harden tokenizer rollout gating with expanded fuzzy-match regression tests.
- Add KV-cache sanity checks during mixed-pool rollouts.
- Expand canary telemetry for token-boundary drift signals.

I'll draft a customer-friendly summary for Monica to send; Jordan/Hannah please add any operations or sales-level notes.

-Aditya
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@bluewave.cap>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@bluewave.cap>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — tokenization mismatch (Apr 10)

Jason / Emily — thank you again for the samples and patience while we investigated. Below is a concise post-incident summary for BlueWave Capital, steps we've taken, and recommended next actions.

1) Impact summary (what happened)
- Between 2027-04-10T15:55:00Z and 2027-04-10T18:50:00Z a rollout of an updated tokenizer (rtkn-v2.4) produced altered token boundaries for a subset of inputs containing certain unicode sequences and emoji. When combined with a KV-cache race during mixed-pool handling, this caused divergent generation results in ~2.3% of batch rows for BlueWave's scoring jobs.

2) Immediate corrective actions we took
- 18:42 UTC — rolled back tokenizer to rtkn-v2.3 across the serving fleet.
- 18:50 UTC — deployed KV-cache sequencing hotfix INF-7123 to ensure fresh KV slices are used after pool changes.
- Reprocessed a representative subsample of your affected batches; differences were reduced to <0.01% compared to pre-incident baselines.

3) Scope and verification
- Affected window: 2027-04-10T15:55:00Z — 2027-04-10T18:50:00Z.
- Based on our logs, ~2.3% of rows for requests routed to mixed-canary pools in that window showed differing outputs. We attached the audit logs and a verification checklist to reproduce validation locally.

4) Customer-facing remediation options
- Option A: We can reprocess impacted batch jobs for you (we will coordinate filenames/ids and provide a redrive plan).
- Option B: If you prefer to re-run on your side, we will supply pre-incident baselines and a validation script.
- Option C: Acceptance of the mitigation and no reprocessing; we'll still provide logs and credits.

5) Proposed credits and follow-ups
- We're prepared to issue a credit equivalent to one week of batch-processing fees for the impacted streams (subject to your confirmation).
- Proposed follow-up: a 30-minute technical sync with Aditya + Hannah to walk through the validation steps and reprocessing plan.

6) Longer-term actions we're committing to
- Gate tokenizer rollouts with expanded unit + fuzzy regression tests for token-boundary drift (ETA: Q3 2027).
- Improve mixed-pool KV-cache sequencing and add automated sanity checks (ETA: 6 weeks).
- Add an incident dashboard tile to surface tokenization-warning spikes to customers in the Console (ETA: Q3 2027).

Attachments: customer-facing-postmortem-20270411.pdf, bluewave-raw-logs-20270410.gz, tokenization-diff-0410.csv

Next steps for BlueWave:
- Reply to this note with which remediation option you prefer (A/B/C) and a list of affected job ids if you choose reprocessing.
- If you'd like the sync, propose 2 slots and we'll confirm availability.

We regret the impact and are prioritizing changes to prevent recurrence. Happy to discuss details on the call.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
